edits.new_text: A cleaning system (R) for bottles (F), particularly glass and/or plastic bottles, comprising a housing in which at least one transport element comprising bottle carriers (H) conveys the bottles (F) through different system zones, wherein at least one sheet-metal wall is provided in the housing as a boundary of the bottle transport path, which sheet-metal wall can be contacted on a bottle contact side by bottles at least in at least one locally defined wear portion (V) along the bottle transport path, and at least one exchangeably arranged wear plate which in the wear portion (V) defines the bottle contact side of the sheet-metal wall is provided in the wear portion (V) of the sheet-metal wall, wherein bottles in transverse rows are conveyed spaced apart from one another with gaps along given bottle paths, and fastening elements for fixing the wear plate are aligned with the gaps between the bottles.
The cleaning system according to claim 1, wherein the wear plate is one of engaged, fixed or a combination thereof with detachable locks in the wear portion (V).
The cleaning system according to claim 1, wherein the wear plate is more wear-resistant than portions of the sheet-metal wall adjacent to the wear plate.

The cleaning system according to claim 1, wherein bottles (F) in each of the transverse rows are conveyed spaced apart from one another with gaps along given bottle paths, and that screws or locks for fixing the wear plate are aligned with the gaps between the bottles (F).
The cleaning system of claim 6, wherein the wear plate and the sheet-metal wall are flush with one another on the bottle contact side.
The cleaning system of claim 7, wherein the wear plate consists of more wear-resistant sheet-metal material than the portions of the sheet-metal wall.

arguments.assertion: The amendments correct the indefinite limitations by providing proper antecedent basis for 'sheet-metal wall' and clarifying that the wear plate and sheet-metal wall are flush with one another, thereby removing the self-referential language objected to by the Examiner.
arguments.support_span: The tightened screws 5 are flush with the bottle contact side or are even countersunk.

arguments.assertion: Amended claim 1 now recites that fastening elements for fixing the wear plate are aligned with gaps between bottles conveyed in transverse rows, a specific structural arrangement adapted for cleaning systems to prevent collisions, which Kronseder does not disclose or suggest.
arguments.support_span: Expediently, screws 5 are aligned with the gaps 12 to rule out objectionable collisions or collisions causing wear, for instance for the bottle bottoms.

arguments.assertion: Kronseder discloses a guide rail system rather than a cleaning system wall subject to abrasive soiling, and fails to teach or suggest aligning fasteners with bottle gaps to mitigate collision-induced wear in a cleaning environment, rendering the claimed combination non-obvious.
arguments.support_span: The local wear is all the more pronounced the more dirt and sand has been introduced into the cleaning system.

response.notes: Claims 7, 15, 20, and 21 are amended to cure 35 U.S.C. 112(b) indefiniteness rejections. Independent claim 1 is further amended to incorporate the gap-alignment feature of claim 15 to overcome the 102/103 rejections over Kronseder. Claim 3 is corrected for a typographical error.

7. A management method by a management apparatus for managing a computer system for providing a host system with logical volumes, which are created respectively in a plurality of storage apparatuses, as virtual volumes in one virtual storage apparatus, the management method comprising: a first step executed by the management apparatus of grouping the respective storage apparatuses constituting the virtual storage apparatus into a plurality of storage groups in accordance with a designated grouping policy and assigning a group ID specific to the storage group, to which the relevant storage apparatus belongs, to each storage apparatus; and a second step executed by the management apparatus when setting a copy pair, a copy pair setting unit used when of switching a part or whole of each of the logical volumes, which are associated with the respective virtual volumes designated as a copy source and a copy destination of the copy pair, to an appropriate logical volume as necessary based on the group ID assigned to each storage apparatus and in accordance with a designated copy pair setting policy, wherein the copy pair setting policy includes a location relationship of the respective logical volumes associated with the respective virtual volumes designated as the copy source and the copy destination, the location relationship being at least one of a first location relationship in which the respective logical volumes exist in the same storage apparatus, a second location relationship in which the respective logical volumes exist in different storage apparatuses belonging to the same storage group, and a third location relationship in which the respective logical volumes exist in storage apparatuses belonging to different storage groups.

edits.new_text: The method of claim 1 wherein depositing metal in the trench and forming an overburden portion of metal overlying the dielectric layer comprises depositing tungsten by a process that minimizes fluorine concentration at a deposition interface.
The method of claim 10 wherein filling the trenches with tungsten comprises depositing tungsten by a process that minimizes fluorine concentration at a deposition interface.

arguments.assertion: Lin teaches an etch-back process for through-silicon vias, not for replacement metal gate structures, and does not recognize that a selective chemical etch can remove metal gate overburden to avoid mechanical planarization. The claimed chemical etch selectively removes the overburden without mechanical forces, solving the specific problem of grain lifting and surface roughness in gate fabrication, which is absent in TSV processing. Choi and Lin do not suggest adapting TSV etch-back to gate fabrication for this purpose.
arguments.support_span: The selective etch process does not utilize any mechanical means, such as an abrasive polishing pad as used m CMP processes, to etch the gate metal 54 Rather, the selective etch process is limited to non- mechanical forces, i e, wet or dry chemical etchants

arguments.assertion: Hirano discloses nitrogen-assisted CVD for lowering deposition temperature and increasing rate, but does not teach or suggest depositing smooth tungsten to achieve a gate surface roughness of less than 0.5 nm. There is no motivation to modify the prior art with Hirano to solve the specific problem of grain lifting and surface roughness in metal gates.
arguments.support_span: The chemical, non-mechanical removal of the overburden portion described herein does not cause grain removal and results m a metal gate with a smoother surface

arguments.assertion: Yamaguchi controls fluorine concentration to improve vapor pressure and deposition rate, not to minimize fluorine at the deposition interface to form smooth tungsten gates. The references fail to teach or suggest the claimed interface fluorine control for avoiding grain lifting and achieving smooth metal gates.
arguments.support_span: An exemplary low fluonne tungsten is deposited by minimizing fluonne concentration at the interface

arguments.assertion: Claims 9 and 15 are amended to recite depositing tungsten by a process that minimizes fluorine concentration at a deposition interface, which is clearly supported by the specification and eliminates the indefiniteness regarding the term low fluorine tungsten.
arguments.support_span: An exemplary low fluonne tungsten is deposited by minimizing fluonne concentration at the interface

response.notes: Affirms the provisional election of Invention I (Claims 1-19) without traverse. Claim 20 remains withdrawn. Amendments to Claims 9 and 15 cure the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) indefiniteness by tracking paragraph [0027] of the specification.

edits.new_text: A method, comprising: receiving, by a server device, one or more service-level agreements (“SLAs”) associated with a subscriber; receiving, by the server device, key performance indicator (“KPI”) information for traffic that traverses one or more nodes of a network; forecasting, by the server device and based on the KPI information, a violation of a particular SLA, of the one or more SLAs; modifying, by the server device, one or more configuration parameters of one or more nodes of the network to mitigate the violation of the particular SLA; and outputting, by the server device and to the subscriber, after modifying the one or more configuration parameters, information that is derived from the KPI information, the derived information being outputted to the subscriber at a slower rate than a rate at which the KPI information is received by the server device, the derived information indicating that the particular SLA was not violated.

A method, comprising: receiving, by a server device and during a particular time period, first key performance indicator (“KPI”) information regarding traffic associated with a subscriber, the first KPI information including a first plurality of values that each correspond to a particular time within the particular time period; providing, by the server device and to a device associated with the subscriber, second KPI information regarding the traffic, the second KPI information including a second plurality of data points that each correspond to a particular time within the particular time period, each data point, of the second plurality of data points, being based on at least two data points of the first plurality of data points; detecting, by the server device and based on the first KPI information, that a particular KPI threshold, associated with the subscriber, has been exceeded; and taking, by the server device and based on the detecting, corrective action, the corrective action causing the second KPI information to reflect that the particular KPI threshold has not been exceeded.

arguments.assertion: Lidstrom, Li, and Wilkinson do not teach or suggest the claimed combination of forecasting an SLA violation based on high-frequency KPI information, modifying network configuration parameters to mitigate the violation, and subsequently outputting derived information at a slower rate that indicates the SLA was not violated. The prior art references fail to disclose using corrective actions in conjunction with aggregated, slower-rate reporting to effectively mask temporary violations from the subscriber such that the reported data reflects compliance.
arguments.support_span: In this manner, the NMS may be able to forecast potential SLA violations before the subscriber receives any indication that an SLA was violated, and may take corrective action, such that the subscriber does not receive an indication that an SLA was violated.

arguments.assertion: Lidstrom and Wilkinson do not teach or suggest providing second KPI information comprising aggregated data points at a slower rate after detecting a threshold exceedance and taking corrective action, wherein the corrective action causes the aggregated second KPI information to reflect that the threshold has not been exceeded. The references lack disclosure of this specific technique for masking temporary threshold breaches from the subscriber via corrective action and data aggregation.
arguments.support_span: while the first two data points in the time period between t2 and t3 (in graph 205) may have exceeded the KPI threshold, the average KPI value (shown at t3 in graph 200), presented to the subscriber, may be below the threshold, based on the corrective action taken.

arguments.assertion: The informalities in claim 17 have been corrected as indicated in the amendments.

response.notes: Amendments incorporate limitations clarifying that the slower-rate derived information is output after corrective action and indicates no SLA violation, distinguishing the claims from the cited prior art.

edits.new_text: A control device configured to control a vehicle drive device including a rotary electric machine provided in a power transfer path that connects between an internal combustion engine and wheels, a first engagement device provided between the internal combustion engine and the rotary electric machine, and a second engagement device provided between the rotary electric machine and the wheels, the control device comprising a controller configured to perform starting control for the internal combustion engine, the starting control raising a rotational speed of the internal combustion engine using a rotational drive force of the rotary electric machine in response to a starting request for the internal combustion engine made with the first engagement device in a disengaged state and with the second engagement device in a direct engagement state, wherein the starting control includes: starting first transition control to cause the first engagement device to transition from the disengaged state to a slipping engagement state after the starting request is made; starting rotational speed control to control the rotary electric machine such that a rotational speed of the rotary electric machine becomes a target rotational speed before the first engagement device transitions from the disengaged state to the slipping engagement state; terminating the rotational speed control and starting torque control to control the rotary electric machine such that an output torque of the rotary electric machine becomes a target torque after the first engagement device transitions from the disengaged state to the slipping engagement state; and causing the second engagement device to transition from a direct engagement state to a slipping engagement state after the torque control is started.

The control device according to claim 1, wherein the starting control includes causing the first engagement device to transition from the slipping engagement state to a direct engagement state after the second engagement device transitions from the direct engagement state to the slipping engagement state.

The control device according to claim 1, wherein the starting control includes starting second transition control to cause the second engagement device to transition from the direct engagement state to the slipping engagement state after the torque control is started.

The control device according to claim 1, wherein: the disengaged state of the first engagement device is a state in which the first engagement device is not producing a transfer torque capacity; the slipping engagement state of the first engagement device is a state in which there is a difference between the rotational speed of the internal combustion engine and the rotational speed of the rotary electric machine with the first engagement device producing a transfer torque capacity; the direct engagement state of the first engagement device is a state in which there is no difference between the rotational speed of the internal combustion engine and the rotational speed of the rotary electric machine with the first engagement device producing a transfer torque capacity; the slipping engagement state of the second engagement device is a state in which there is a difference between rotational speeds of two engagement members of the second engagement device with the second engagement device producing a transfer torque capacity; and the direct engagement state of the second engagement device is a state in which there is no difference between the rotational speeds of the two engagement members of the second engagement device with the second engagement device producing a transfer torque capacity.

The control device according to claim 4, wherein the first transition control is started by providing the first engagement device with a command to produce a transfer torque capacity; and the second transition control in which the second engagement device is caused to transition from the direct engagement state to the slipping engagement state is started by providing a command to gradually reduce the transfer torque capacity produced by the second engagement device until there is a difference between the rotational speeds of the two engagement members of the second engagement device.

The control device according to claim 1, wherein after the second engagement device transitions from the direct engagement state to the slipping engagement state, the torque control is terminated, and slipping rotational speed control in which the output torque of the rotary electric machine is controlled so as to bring the rotational speed of the rotary electric machine closer to the target rotational speed which is higher than the rotational speed of the rotary electric machine for a case where the second engagement device is in the direct engagement state is started.

The control device according to claim 1, wherein the second transition control in which the second engagement device is caused to transition from the direct engagement state to the slipping engagement state is started after transfer torque information that is information indicating that the transfer torque capacity of the first engagement device has become equal to or more than a predetermined value is detected.

The control device according to claim 7, wherein information indicating that the rotational speed of the internal combustion engine has become equal to or more than a predetermined rotational speed is used as the transfer torque information.

The control device according to claim 1, wherein the rotational speed control includes: estimating transfer path input torque that is torque input to the power transfer path on the basis of variations in rotational speed of the rotary electric machine; estimating external input torque input from the wheels to the power transfer path by subtracting at least the output torque of the rotary electric machine from the transfer path input torque; and calculating the target rotational speed on the basis of the external input torque and vehicle required torque that is torque required to drive the wheels.

The control device according to claim 1, wherein it is determined that the second engagement device has transitioned from the direct engagement state to the slipping engagement state on the basis of a fact that the rotational speed difference across the second engagement device has become equal to or more than a predetermined value.

arguments.assertion: Claims 1-10 have been rewritten to overcome the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection by adopting a proper one-sentence format with a clear preamble, transition phrase, and sequentially listed functional steps, thereby clearly specifying the operative structure and control sequence as requested by the examiner.
arguments.support_span: The claim(s) are narrative in form and replete with indefinite language. The structure which goes to make up the device must be clearly and positively specified. The structure must be organized and correlated in such a manner as to present a complete operative device. The claim(s) must be in one sentence form only.

response.notes: Claims were restructured to comply with the examiner's explicit instruction to place them in one-sentence form and clearly specify the controller and starting control steps, removing the narrative style while preserving the original technical limitations.

arguments.assertion: Szoke fails to disclose a second resistor connected in parallel with the first resistor specifically to diagnose a control signal line defect by detecting the resistor's availability. Szoke's 'switchable load 34' is not a diagnostic resistor, nor does Szoke teach that an open control signal line renders a second parallel resistor unavailable to indicate a defect.
arguments.support_span: If the control signal line is defective, then the second resistor is ultimately replaced by an infinitely large resistance, so that only the first resistor is actually seen in the parallel circuit, which causes a change in the measured voltage.

arguments.assertion: The 103 rejections rely on Szoke as the primary reference, which fails to disclose the claimed parallel diagnostic resistor arrangement. Combining Szoke with Plagens or Soma is improper because neither secondary reference teaches using parallel resistors to detect control signal line defects based on resistor availability.
arguments.support_span: As per claim 12, Szoke discloses the diagnostic device of claim 11 as described above except wherein the first resistor and the second resistor have identical resistance values.

arguments.assertion: A terminal disclaimer has been filed to overcome the provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection over copending Application No. 14/412,627.

response.notes: Terminal disclaimer submitted to address provisional double patenting. Arguments challenge the 102 and 103 rejections over Szoke, Plagens, and Soma based on the distinct parallel-resistor diagnostic configuration.

arguments.assertion: Hutchins discloses a gas-generating gel system that requires a gas precursor (e.g., urea) reacting with a delayed-acting substance to produce CO2 in situ for crosslinking or bubble formation, whereas the claimed invention utilizes a direct chemical interaction among the silicate, non-crosslinked polymer, and organic reactive carbonyl initiator without any gas precursor or in situ gas generation.
arguments.support_span: In the absence of sodium silicate, polyacrylamide (at neutral pH) did not react with glyoxal or propylene carbonate. In the absence of a "reactive carbonyl" initiator, sodium silicate did not react with polyacrylamide.

arguments.assertion: Hutchins explicitly teaches the use of "crosslinkable polymers," while the claims expressly recite a "non-crosslinked water dispersible polymer," which operates through a fundamentally different gelation mechanism and yields distinct gel properties as described in the specification.
arguments.support_span: The polymeric materials which are suitable for use in the practice of the compositions and methods of the present disclosure include at least one chemically non-crosslinked, water dispersible polymer selected from the group consisting of polyacrylamides and related polymers

response.notes: Claim 19 is canceled to overcome the 35 U.S.C. 112(d) rejection. Arguments address the 102(b) and 103(a) rejections over Hutchins by highlighting the absence of a gas precursor/urea system in the claims and the explicit requirement for a non-crosslinked polymer, which distinguishes the claimed synergistic three-component gel system from Hutchins' gas-crosslinking or bubble-gel teachings.

edits.new_text: 1. A superconducting toroidal magnet made from epitaxially deposited superconductor tapes, wherein a superconductor tape width is adjusted poloidally from an inner leg to an outer leg and radially from an inner bore to a periphery so that, when used in the magnet, the margin, defined as a ratio between the operating current and the critical current, is relatively constant throughout the coil.

arguments.assertion: The proposed combination of MIT and Young lacks a proper motivation because Young teaches a magnet using conventional NbTi strands embedded in copper, which cannot be slit to adjust tape width poloidally without severing filaments, rendering the combination technically infeasible.
arguments.support_span: This approach is unique to YBCO 2nd generation tapes and similar tapes, such as ReBCO; it is not feasible with conventional strands or with tape with MgB2 or BSCCO superconductor (with filaments), as the filaments would be severed during the cutting process.

arguments.assertion: MIT discloses a double pancake coil with multi-width tapes graded radially to match local fields, but does not teach or suggest the claimed poloidal grading along a continuous toroidal turn from an inner leg to an outer leg and from an inner bore to a periphery.
arguments.support_span: In toroidal magnets, the magnetic field is highest at the low major radius, and decreases towards the outer region... grading can also be obtained by varying the widths of tapes as they wrap around the toroid

arguments.assertion: Kobayashi does not teach a hybrid magnet comprising shells that produce a 1/r field combined with radial plates that provide additional currents to maintain a near-constant magnetic field in the bore; rather, Kobayashi relies on winding different HTS tapes in series to shape the field profile.
arguments.support_span: It is a superconducting coil having a pancake shape in which a tape-shaped RE123 superconducting wire and a tape-shaped (Bi,Pb)2223 superconducting wire are connected in series

arguments.assertion: The claimed radial plates serve a distinct electromagnetic function of introducing currents to flatten the field profile, which is fundamentally different from the material-dependent field shaping taught in Kobayashi and not suggested by the reference.
arguments.support_span: An alternative approach is to use a hybrid magnet, using a shell winding, that establishes the 1/R toroidal field, in combinations with radial or near radial plates that generate the near constant toroidal field in the bore of the magnet.

response.notes: Claim 1 has been amended to incorporate the toroidal geometry and specific grading directions taught in the specification, which distinguishes the claimed invention from MIT's solenoidal/double-pancake teaching and overcomes the incompatibility with Young's conventional strand conductor. Claims 2-4 and 6 are maintained but now depend on the amended independent claim. Arguments for claim 10 emphasize that Kobayashi's field shaping mechanism relies on series-connected different superconductors, not the claimed hybrid shell-and-radial-plate architecture.

arguments.assertion: Amended claim 1 now incorporates the allowable limitation regarding the sub upper face and the space therebelow. The Examiner explicitly indicated that these features have not been found, taught, or suggested by the prior art of record, rendering the amended claim patentable over Gasvoda and Gilson.
arguments.support_span: It is these features found in the claim(s) which have not been found, taught or suggested by the prior art of record, which makes these claims allowable over the prior art.

arguments.assertion: A terminal disclaimer will be submitted to overcome the provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection over copending Application No. 14/838438, as permitted by the applicable regulations.
arguments.support_span: A timely filed terminal disclaimer in compliance with 37 CFR 1.321(c) or 1.321(d) may be used to overcome an actual or provisional rejection based on nonstatutory double patenting

response.notes: Terminal disclaimer form will be filed concurrently with this reply.

A method for operating an electronic device, the method comprising: establishing a communication channel to an external electronic device; obtaining a communication profile required for operating a second communication module that supports a communication service provided via a base station using the external electronic device connected; storing the communication profile obtained; and receiving selection information indicating at least one of a service contract option and a communication profile selected from subscription support information received from the external electronic device.

Tamura's cited paragraphs only disclose Bluetooth hardware profiles (DUN and HF) for routing data and audio signals, and do not teach selecting cellular service contracts or obtaining communication profiles via subscription support information as required by the amended claims.
arguments.support_span: According to various embodiments of the present disclosure, the control module may receive selection information on a service contract option or a communication profile selected from the subscription support information received from the external electronic device.
